items.title: Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now provides business users visibility into resiliency readiness across linked Regions
items.summary:
Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency now provides a Global Resiliency page in the admin website, giving administrators a single place to review their Region switch readiness. The page shows an overall readiness status and lists the resources that Global Resiliency natively replicates, including which resource types are in sync, which are still pending synchronization, and which need action. For example, if a phone number or user is not associated with a traffic distribution group, the page flags it and lets the administrator associate the affected resources directly from the page. With this readiness overview, administrators can review their resiliency posture at any time and verify that their instance is ready for a Region switch.
This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer Global Resiliency is supported. To learn more, see Amazon Connect Customer admin guide.

items.title: Amazon CloudWatch Omni is now available in additional AWS Regions
items.summary:
AWS announces that Amazon CloudWatch Omni is now available in eight additional AWS Regions. CloudWatch Omni is an AI-powered observability experience, organized around your teams and the applications they run, that helps you observe and troubleshoot your applications and agents in one place. It combines the interoperability of OpenTelemetry with the scale and reliability of CloudWatch, and meets you where you work — a standalone web experience with single sign-on (SSO), or a local IDE extension.
With CloudWatch Omni, You create spaces in your central accounts to see telemetry across your AWS accounts, Regions, and other clouds, including Azure and GCP. Omni discovers services, maps dependencies, and surfaces golden metrics automatically and you can interact with telemetry through chat, point-and-click, or your own tool via Agent Toolkit for AWS to find signals, build dynamic views, and reach root cause powered by AWS DevOps Agent. A dedicated agent observability experience adds an evaluation-driven workflow for frameworks including LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Vercel AI SDK, and Strands.
With this expansion, CloudWatch Omni is now available in Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), and South America (São Paulo), in addition to US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Europe (Ireland).
To get started, create your Omni space from the CloudWatch console, configure SSO, and sign in. Agent developers can install the free CloudWatch Omni extension for VS Code, Cursor, and Kiro. To learn more, see the Amazon CloudWatch Omni product page and documentation. For pricing, see the CloudWatch Omni pricing page.

items.title: EC2 Image Builder now integrates with ASG for faster image builds
items.summary:
EC2 Image Builder now supports using existing instances from an Auto Scaling Group (ASG) for building images, enabling faster builds by eliminating the time spent in launching and bootstrapping new instances and reusing already running EC2 instances.
With this feature, you can provide an ASG in your Image Builder infrastructure configuration. Instead of launching a new instance at the build time, Image Builder selects an already-running instance from this ASG, applies your build components, and creates the image. The ASG continuously replenishes the pool as instances are used for builds, ensuring instances are always available for subsequent pipeline runs.
This feature is fully opt-in and does not affect existing pipelines. Pipelines without an ASG configured continue to use the default launch path with no behavior change.
This feature is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost. To configure ASG integration in your Image Builder pipelines, see the EC2 Image Builder documentation.

items.title: Amazon GuardDuty adds optional threat detection rules for Runtime Monitoring
items.summary:
Amazon GuardDuty now supports optional detection rules for Runtime Monitoring. You can enable more than 50 Runtime Monitoring rules that help detect process, file, and network activity that might be routine in one environment but a sign of compromise in another, such as modifying sudoers files or disabling audit logging.
The new rules provide detections for Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon EKS, and Amazon ECS on both EC2 and AWS Fargate, and span 13 finding types mapped to MITRE ATT&CK® tactics including persistence, privilege escalation, execution, defense evasion, discovery, exfiltration, and command and control. This release introduces four new finding types: CommandAndControl:Runtime/SuspiciousCommand, CredentialAccess:Runtime/SensitiveFileRead, Discovery:Runtime/SensitiveFileRead, and Exfiltration:Runtime/SuspiciousCommand.
To get started, visit the GuardDuty console. You can enable rules in dry-run mode to evaluate detection efficacy before enabling live detection.
Custom Detection Rules for Runtime Monitoring is available in all AWS commercial Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, see Amazon GuardDuty Custom Detection Rules. To receive programmatic updates on new Amazon GuardDuty features and threat detections, subscribe to the Amazon GuardDuty SNS topic.

AWS Lambda learned to run a plain HTTP server with no adapter in front of it, and Amazon S3 became something you can provision from inside the […]

items.title: Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary:
Amazon Bedrock now supports SpaceXAI Grok 4.7, a frontier model built for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work in AWS GovCloud (US).
Grok 4.7 builds on Grok 4.6 with better mixed-document handling, more dependable repo-scale coding with planning and error recovery, and enhanced browser-use agents for form fills and portal navigation.  
Get started with Grok 4.7 in the Amazon Bedrock console or programmatically through supported Amazon Bedrock APIs. For information about supported AWS Regions, endpoints, APIs, features, inference profiles and pricing, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation. To learn more, read the launch blog post.

items.title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports optimistic locking for users and groups in its identity store
items.summary:
IAM Identity Center helps you configure the single sign-on experience of your workforce to AWS accounts and applications. You can now use optimistic locking for users and groups in the identity store, so that update and delete requests succeed only if the user or group hasn't changed since you last read it. This helps when multiple administrators or automated workflows modify the same user or group at nearly the same time, where previously one write could silently overwrite another.
 
Identity Store API Reference.

items.title: AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports high bitrate mode
items.summary:
AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports high bitrate modes with two new tiers: 250 Mbps and 500 Mbps. This allows professional broadcasters that need higher bitrates to transport high-value content without compromising quality or reliability.
This enhancement enables industry-standard workflows such as VSF TR-07 compliant transport stream distribution for broadcast contribution, content distribution, and remote production. High bitrate mode supports up to two redundant sources for reliability and includes data plane optimizations that reduce jitter for improved performance.
To learn more, visit the AWS Elemental MediaConnect product page and the MediaConnect pricing page.

items.title: Amazon RDS Custom now supports the latest Cumulative Update and GDR updates for Microsoft SQL Server
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) Custom for SQL Server now supports the latest Cumulative Updates (CU) and General Distribution Release (GDR) updates for Microsoft SQL Server. This release includes support for SQL Server 2019 CU32+GDR KB5122772(RDS version 15.00.4490.9.v1) and SQL Server 2022 CU26 + GDR KB5122768 (RDS version 16.00.4275.2.v1).
 
Amazon RDS Custom User Guide.

items.title: Amazon RDS for SQL Server now supports snapshots on read replicas
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports creating DB snapshots directly on read replica instances. Previously, you could create snapshots only on standalone and primary DB instances. You can now snapshot a read replica without promoting it first, giving you more flexibility in your backup and disaster recovery (DR) workflows.
Previously, enabling Multi-AZ on a promoted read replica meant waiting for an initial full snapshot to finish before the conversion could begin. On larger storage configurations—such as io2 volumes up to 64 TiB—that first snapshot could take a long time, making DR timelines hard to predict. Now, Amazon RDS for SQL Server maintains snapshot data on the read replica throughout its lifecycle, so the first snapshot after promotion completes faster. This shortens the time to enable Multi-AZ and helps you plan DR exercises with more predictable recovery timelines. You can take manual snapshots of a read replica, turn on automated backups by setting a backup retention period greater than zero, and retain automated backups when you delete the replica; however, point-in-time recovery (PITR) from a read replica isn't supported.
This feature works for both in-region and cross-region read replicas. It's available for SQL Server Enterprise Edition on all SQL Server versions that support read replicas, in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for SQL Server read replicas are available, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions.
To learn more, see Working with read replicas for Microsoft SQL Server. For pricing details, see Amazon RDS for SQL Server Pricing.

items.title: AWS Partner Central adds Solution Matching Engine performance insights
items.summary:
AWS Partner Central now gives AWS Partners more visibility into how the Solution Matching Engine (SME) contributes to their co-sell pipeline. The Solution Matching Engine performance section in Partner Analytics helps partners understand how SME performs for their company and AWS Marketplace listings.
Partners can view recommendations, SME-attributed opportunities, their share of AWS-originated opportunities, stall rate, and pipeline attributed to SME. They can filter by recommendation type or AWS Marketplace listing and explore top customer profiles by Region, industry, and segment. These insights help partners assess their visibility and decide where to improve their listings and opportunity information.
All partners eligible for APN Customer Engagements (ACE) can find the section on the Opportunity pipeline analysis page under Partner Analytics in AWS Partner Central. To learn more about SME and how to strengthen your visibility with AWS sellers, read Solution Matching Engine: Your Gateway to AWS Sellers.

items.title: Amazon CloudWatch log centralization now available in AWS GovCloud and additional commercial Regions
items.summary:
Amazon CloudWatch log centralization is now available in AWS GovCloud (US) and 13 additional commercial Regions. CloudWatch log centralization copies log data from multiple AWS accounts and Regions into a single destination account, integrating with AWS Organizations for efficient aggregation without the need for custom solutions.
With this launch, organizations in the AWS GovCloud (US) partition and commercial partition can each centralize logs across their accounts and Regions for centralized monitoring. You can scope centralization rules to your entire organization, specific organizational units, or selected accounts and copy logs into a single account while preserving source context through enriched system fields.
CloudWatch log centralization is now additionally available in Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Canada West (Calgary), Europe (Milan), Europe (Spain), Europe (Zurich), Israel (Tel Aviv), Middle East (Bahrain), Middle East (UAE), AWS GovCloud (US-East), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). For a complete list of supported Regions, see the AWS Region table.
To get started, create a centralization rule in the Amazon CloudWatch console, or by using the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs. To learn more, see Log centralization in the Amazon CloudWatch Logs User Guide. Customers can centralize one copy of logs for free; additional copies are charged at $0.05/GB. For details, see Amazon CloudWatch pricing.

items.title: Amazon EMR Serverless now supports IPv6 and dual-stack connectivity
items.summary:
Amazon EMR Serverless now supports IPv6 and dual-stack connectivity, expanding beyond the IPv4-only connectivity that was previously available. You can now run your Apache Spark and Apache Hive jobs over IPv6 in your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) by supplying dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) or IPv6-only subnets. This gives you greater flexibility in how your applications connect to data stores and services, while maintaining full backward compatibility with your existing IPv4 workloads.
As Spark and Hive workloads scale to many workers, the IPv4 address space in your VPCs and subnets can become a constraint, and a growing number of organizations face compliance mandates that require IPv6 adoption. With dual-stack connectivity, your EMR Serverless applications accept both IPv4 and IPv6, making it easy to adopt IPv6 gradually while maintaining backward compatibility with your existing IPv4 workloads. With IPv6-only subnets, you can eliminate the need for IPv4 addresses entirely, overcoming IPv4 address exhaustion and meeting the networking standards and compliance requirements that call for IPv6, while your jobs reach IPv6 endpoints and services both inside and outside your VPC.
IPv6 and dual-stack connectivity for Amazon EMR Serverless is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon EMR Serverless is available. IPv6 and dual-stack subnets are supported on all EMR Serverless release versions. To get started, see Configure IPv6 subnets for EMR Serverless applications and Configuring VPC access for EMR Serverless applications.

items.title: AWS Lambda durable functions are now available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
items.summary:
AWS Lambda durable functions are now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) and AWS GovCloud (US-East) Regions. Lambda durable functions enable developers to build reliable multi-step applications and AI workflows within the Lambda developer experience.
Lambda durable functions extend the Lambda programming model with new primitives in your event handler, such as "step" and "wait", allowing you to checkpoint progress, automatically recover from failures, and pause executions without incurring compute charges for on-demand functions. With availability in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, government customers and regulated industries can orchestrate complex processes such as order workflows, user onboarding, and AI-assisted tasks while meeting stringent compliance and security requirements.
You can activate durable functions for new Python (versions 3.13 and 3.14), Node.js (versions 22 and 24), Go (versions 1.24 or later), .Net (version 2.2), or Java (17+) based Lambda functions using the AWS Lambda API, AWS Management Console, or AWS SDK. You can also use infrastructure as code tools such as AWS CloudFormation, AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM), and the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK).
For more information on durable functions, visit the AWS Lambda durable functions product page or the AWS Lambda Developer Guide. To learn about pricing, visit AWS Lambda pricing. For region availability, visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page.

items.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
items.summary:
NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, expanding the portfolio of foundation models available to AWS customers. This vision-language model from the Nemotron 3.5 family accepts images, video, and text as input and generates text, enabling customers to deploy multimodal AI solutions on AWS infrastructure.
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is designed for document intelligence, GUI understanding, video question answering, and multimodal agentic applications. It pairs a 120B-parameter hybrid Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language backbone with 12B active parameters and a vision encoder, supporting context lengths of up to 1 million tokens. The model includes a built-in Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) head for speculative decoding to accelerate text generation, with reasoning configurable per request. It supports ten languages including English, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, Hindi, Korean, and Chinese. Post-trained with multimodal supervised fine-tuning on image, video, document, chart, and GUI data followed by GRPO reinforcement learning, it delivers structured JSON output, tool calling, and configurable reasoning for enterprise agent workflows. SageMaker JumpStart offers two variants: NVFP4 for optimized inference on G7 instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, and BF16 reference weights on ml.p5en.48xlarge for customization including SFT, RL, distillation, and domain adaptation.
With SageMaker JumpStart, customers can deploy Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with just a few clicks to address their specific AI use cases.
To get started with these models, navigate to the SageMaker JumpStart model catalog in the SageMaker console or use the SageMaker Python SDK to deploy the models to your AWS account. For more information about deploying and using foundation models in SageMaker JumpStart, see the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart documentation.

items.title: Beam model by Reflection is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart and AWS Trainium
items.summary:
Beam, the first open weight model offered by US-based Reflection, is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, the model hub in Amazon SageMaker AI. According to Beam, they operate at the frontier of open weight models in its class, with strong performance across reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks. With it, customers can now build advanced coding agents and automated workflows on a frontier open weight model while keeping control of their data and infrastructure and adapting the model to their business. Beam runs alongside other models that customers already use in SageMaker AI and scales to meet production demand with the same controls, audit trails, and monitoring built into every SageMaker AI deployment. Additionally, Beam was ported and optimized for AWS Trainium3, giving customers a high-performance, cost-efficient option for deploying and scaling the model from day one. “Reflection is delivering frontier AI that developers can actually control, not just rent through an API. Bringing Beam to SageMaker AI puts that capability in front of millions of developers on infrastructure they already trust, running in their own AWS account, on their own data, fully in their control," said Misha Laskin, co-founder and CEO, Reflection.
Engineering teams can use Beam to resolve software issues, generate and review code, and automate routine operations work. Businesses can also use it for complex workflows that span many steps and tools, and for advanced math and science reasoning. Because Beam is released under the Apache 2.0 license, customers can inspect and customize the model, while also running it in their own AWS accounts, so data stays private and under their control, protected by the same AWS security and compliance capabilities they already rely on.  “Advanced AI models like Beam, now available on Amazon SageMaker, let us run open weight frontier AI entirely inside our own secure environments, with full visibility into the weights, the data, and the pipeline. In the age of multi-model AI, the pairing of openness and managed infrastructure is an essential addition to the AI ecosystem. The freedom to deploy and adapt advanced AI, tailored to mission problems with client-specific security and controls, gives more agencies greater flexibility to deploy advanced AI across their enterprise." said Garrett Berntsen, Chief AI Officer, Accenture Federal Services.
Beam is initially available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart in US East (N. Virginia) and US East (Ohio). To start, search for "Beam" in SageMaker JumpStart within Amazon SageMaker Studio, or deploy it directly on SageMaker AI.  To learn more, read the AWS/Beam launch blog, SageMaker AI documentation and SageMaker JumpStart documentation.

items.title: AWS Transform announces Azure-to-AWS cloud-native code conversion
items.summary:
Today, AWS announced the general availability of application code conversion from Azure SDK to AWS SDK in AWS Transform, giving you an accelerated path to migrate Microsoft Azure cloud-native .NET applications to AWS. The AWS Transform .NET modernization agent identifies Azure service code and converts it to equivalent AWS service code. For example, an Azure Functions serverless function that uses Azure Cosmos DB can be converted to an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon DynamoDB.
AWS Transform discovers the Azure SDK in your submitted source code and presents the conversion options in the assessment report and modernization plan. You can accept the options provided or adjust them based on your preferences before running the modernization. AWS Transform then converts the identified Azure service code to the equivalent AWS SDK calls, and validates that the changes are incorporated into the transformed code. The feature supports conversion of Azure Functions to AWS Lambda functions, Azure Blob Storage to Amazon S3, and Azure Queue Storage to Amazon SQS, with Azure Cosmos DB to Amazon DynamoDB conversion available in preview.
AWS Transform is available in eight AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney), Canada (Central), and Europe (Frankfurt, London).
To learn more, see Convert cloud-native code to AWS in the AWS Transform User Guide.

items.title: Amazon Braket now in scope for FedRAMP Class C
items.summary:
Amazon Braket is now in scope for FedRAMP Class C in AWS US Regions where Braket is available. The Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) is a US government-wide program that delivers a standard approach to the security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring of cloud products and services.
With FedRAMP Class C authorization, government customers and the organizations that serve them can use Amazon Braket to explore quantum computing within an authorized boundary. The AWS-operated components of Braket, including the API and SDK, job orchestration and management, compilation, and result storage in Amazon S3, are within the FedRAMP-certified boundary, while quantum workloads execute on third-party Quantum Hardware Providers (QHPs) outside that boundary. All data sent to QHPs meets AWS' privacy and security requirements including removal of all personally identifiable information, data encryption in transit and at rest, and adherence to AWS' standard data retention and deletion policies.
To learn more about FedRAMP, visit AWS FedRAMP services and the FedRAMP Marketplace. To learn more about Amazon Braket, visit the Braket product page and Getting Started on Braket resources.
Regional Availability: US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon)

items.title: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks now supported in the AWS Mexico (Central) Region
items.summary:
Second-generation AWS Outposts racks are now supported in the AWS Mexico (Central) Region. Outposts racks extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to virtually any on-premises data center or colocation space for a truly consistent hybrid experience. 
 
To learn more about second-generation Outposts racks, read the blog post and the user guide. For the latest list of countries and territories and the AWS Regions where second-generation Outposts racks are supported, see the Outposts rack FAQs page.

items.title: AWS End User Messaging adds registration improvements for faster, higher-quality submissions
items.summary:
AWS End User Messaging now makes it easier to complete messaging registrations correctly the first time, with clearer guidance, explicit field requirements, and help avoiding the most common rejection reasons. Registrations ask for compliance evidence such as opt-in proof and sample messages, and submissions are often delayed or denied when that evidence is incomplete or a required field is missed. These improvements give you worked examples, surface exactly which fields you must provide, and walk you through the content that most often causes denials.
 
User Guide.

items.title: AWS End User Messaging now supports Brand Profiles
items.summary:
Today, AWS End User Messaging announces Brand Profiles, which let you store your brand and company information once and reuse it across your messaging registrations. To send messages on SMS, RCS, and WhatsApp, you register your brand with carriers and messaging providers, and today you fill in the same company details, address, contact information, and use case by hand on every form, for each channel and country. That repeated entry slows every new registration, and a typo or other error can get one rejected and delay when you can start sending. With Brand Profiles, you enter this information once and apply it to each new registration, so you register faster and keep your details consistent across channels and countries. You can use Brand Profiles whether you send for your own brand or manage several brands in a single AWS account.
 
User Guide.

items.title: AWS End User Messaging adds a guided wizard for RCS registration videos
items.summary:
Today, AWS End User Messaging adds a wizard that orchestrates the entire video capture for your RCS agent registration. RCS registrations in multiple countries, including the United States, require a screen recording that demonstrates your messaging experience. To record it, you have to send a specific sequence of messages to a test device, and until now you scripted those messages yourself, which easily introduced errors and made a mismatched or incomplete video one of the hardest parts of registering for RCS.
 
User Guide.

items.title: AWS End User Messaging now offers managed OTP verification end-to-end
items.summary:
Today, AWS End User Messaging announces end-to-end managed one-time passcode (OTP) verification in Notify. You get a working OTP solution in under five minutes, including AWS phone numbers and code verification, without setting up a phone number, registering with carriers, or managing how messages are delivered. Before, you generated the passcode yourself and passed it to Notify to send, and you built and maintained the logic to create, store, and expire codes. Now Notify generates the code, delivers it, and verifies the code the recipient enters, so you ship a complete verification flow and skip that work entirely. You can deliver codes over text, voice, and now WhatsApp.
 
User Guide.

items.title: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore expands to AWS GovCloud and 3 Regions
items.summary:
Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now available in four additional AWS Regions: US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). Web Search is a fully managed tool that provides AI agents with current grounding from the web, enabling more accurate and up-to-date responses for tasks such as research, summarization, and question answering.
With this expansion, customers can build agents that retrieve web information closer to their applications and end users with lower latency. Customers with government workloads can now use Web Search in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region to meet compliance and data residency requirements. 
To learn more about Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, see the Web Search tool documentation. To learn about pricing, visit Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing. For Region availability, visit Supported AWS Regions.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Studio simplifies getting started for new AI/ML builders with new sign-in options
items.summary:
Amazon SageMaker Studio now lets new customers sign up with their Google, GitHub, or Apple credentials and land inside a fully configured Studio environment - no traditional AWS account setup and no console navigation required.
Previously, new customers who discovered a model on Hugging Face or an AWS product page had to complete a multi-step AWS account creation process, provide a credit card, navigate the AWS Console to find SageMaker AI, configure an environment, and set up IAM permissions before they could begin working. With earlier launches, we reduced environment setup to twenty seconds, pre-configured model customization permissions, and introduced deep links from Hugging Face and AWS product pages so customers could land directly inside Studio with a model pre-loaded. Now, with new sign-in options, customers complete a simplified sign-up using an existing identity, receive free credits as part of the AWS Free Tier with no credit card required in most cases, and arrive inside a ready-to-use SageMaker Studio environment where they can immediately fine-tune, evaluate, and deploy foundation models. Customers can invite team members by email, and collaborators sign in with their own email credentials to access the shared Studio environment, including shared models, notebooks, and endpoints without configuring IAM users or permissions. When a project grows beyond free credits, customers can upgrade to a paid plan and set a spend limit to stay within budget. Verified customers continue to receive default GPU access to G5, G6, G6e, and G4dn instances across endpoint deployments, training jobs, and notebooks without requesting quota increases.
This feature is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where Amazon SageMaker Studio is supported. To get started, visit any supported model on Hugging Face and select "Customize and Deploy on SageMaker AI" or "Deploy on SageMaker AI," or click Get Started from the SageMaker Studio page. To learn more, see the AWS sign-up documentation and SageMaker Studio setup guide.

items.title: Amazon EC2 T8i instances are now available in South America (São Paulo)
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) T8i instances are now available in South America (São Paulo). These instances are powered by custom sixth generation Intel Xeon 6 processors, available exclusively on AWS, and built on the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards. T8i instances deliver up to 30% better price performance compared to previous generation T3 instances, and offer four sizes: nano, micro, small, and medium. These instances are designed for workloads requiring low to moderate CPU utilization, including data processing, login gateways, small databases, batch processing, event driven functions, CI/CD pipelines, microservices, and low traffic websites.
 
AWS Free Tier. T8i instances are available in US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon, N. California), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Paris), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad, Malaysia, Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo), Canada (Central) and South America (São Paulo) regions. T8i instances are available to purchase via On-Demand instances, and Spot instances with Savings Plan option coming soon. To learn more, visit the Amazon EC2 T8i instances page.

items.title: AWS Transform for migrations is now available in Asia Pacific (Singapore)
items.summary:
AWS Transform for migrations is now available in the Asia Pacific (Singapore) Region, giving customers data residency within the region and lower latency to local source infrastructure as they migrate. AWS Transform is a collaborative enterprise IT transformation service powered by agentic AI that accelerates cloud migration, application modernization, and continuous tech debt reduction.
 
documentation or visit the AWS Transform product page.

items.title: Amazon DynamoDB Streams now supports timestamp-based stream processing
items.summary:
Amazon DynamoDB Streams now supports timestamp-based stream processing, enabling you to begin reading stream records from a specific point in time. Previously, you could only start from the oldest retained record (up to 24 hours old) or from new records written after you start consuming the stream. Now, you can supply a timestamp and begin processing at the first record written at or after that time using the AT_TIMESTAMP shard iterator type.
Timestamp-based stream processing can be used with the Amazon Kinesis Client Library (KCL) through the DynamoDB Streams Kinesis adapter. It helps you avoid reprocessing entire retained streams or missing records when resuming stream consumption, supporting common use cases such as recovery after an interruption, data replay for debugging and auditing by reading from a specific point in the past, skipping a backlog by resuming from a recent timestamp near the latest records, and synchronizing after a restore by beginning at the export timestamp following a point-in-time recovery (PITR) export.
Timestamp-based stream processing is available in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the China Regions. There is no additional charge for this feature beyond standard GetRecords API request charges. To get started, see Amazon DynamoDB Streams timestamp documentation in the DynamoDB developer guide.

items.title: AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Go is now generally available
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces the general availability of the AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Go, enabling Go developers to build resilient, long-running workflows using Lambda durable functions. With this SDK, developers can create multi-step applications like infrastructure automation, deployment rollouts with approval gates, and pipelines that call AI models and pause for human review directly in their Go code without implementing custom progress tracking.
Lambda durable functions extend Lambda's event-driven programming model with operations that checkpoint progress automatically and pause execution for up to an year when waiting on external events. The AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Go provides a native Go experience for building with Lambda durable functions. It includes steps for progress tracking, callback integration for human and agent-in-the-loop workflows, durable invocation for reliable function chaining, and waits for efficient suspension.
The SDK works with the Go tools developers already use. Developers add it to a Go module with go get and deploy their function as a single static binary on the provided.al2023 runtime, like any other Go function on Lambda. Before deploying, they can locally test complete workflows on their own machine with the durabletest package, without requiring network access or AWS credentials, and use the durablelint analyzer to catch code that could break a workflow when it resumes.
To get started, see the Lambda durable functions developer guide and the AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Go on GitHub. For Regional availability and pricing details for Lambda durable functions, see the AWS Capabilities by Region page and AWS Lambda Pricing.

items.title: Muse Spark Open model now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
items.summary:
Meta's Muse Spark Open is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, expanding the portfolio of foundation models available to AWS customers. This coding-optimized open-weight model from Meta is purpose-built for agentic coding workflows, bringing multi-step reasoning and tool calling to enterprise software engineering on AWS infrastructure.
Muse Spark Open is designed for long-running coding agents and multimodal engineering workflows. Built on a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with 816B total parameters and 42B active per token, it delivers the capacity of a very large network while keeping per-token compute closer to that of a much smaller dense model. The model holds a 1M-token context window, enabling it to ingest an entire project—including dependencies, legacy code, and thousands of files—without splitting tasks into smaller pieces. It accepts text, images, documents, audio, and audio-video as input and generates text output. Trained on real developer workflows such as multi-file refactors and long debugging sessions, it plans, acts, observes results, and self-corrects over long horizons rather than making single tool calls. SageMaker JumpStart offers two variants: BF16 (Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B) and NVFP4 quantized (Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4), with the NVFP4 variant requiring roughly a quarter of the memory for cost-efficient deployment.
With SageMaker JumpStart, customers can deploy Muse Spark Open with just a few clicks, with the endpoint running in their own AWS account for full control over source code and prompts.
To get started with this model, navigate to the SageMaker JumpStart model catalog in the SageMaker console or use the SageMaker Python SDK to deploy the model to your AWS account. For more information about deploying and using foundation models in SageMaker JumpStart, see the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart documentation.
